newsitem.title: USA: Gunman shoots four at Oregon Scientology office.
newsitem.headline: Gunman shoots four at Oregon Scientology office.

text.p: A man police identifed as a Kenyan with a history of conflict with the Church of Scientology was held for allegedly shooting a pregant woman and three others at a church office on Wednesday.
The woman, 44, about four months' pregnant, was in critical condition with a shoulder wound and "abdominal trauma," said Annette Semper of Oregon Health Sciences University Hospital.
Two men were in serious condition and a third was in fair condition, all with gunshot wounds, she said.
Police spokesman Lt. Cliff Madison said the gunman walked into the storefront church office in downtown Portland shortly before noon (3 p.m. EDT) and opened fire.
While office workers escaped out a back door, the gunman poured gasoline on the floor and set a fire, Madison said. The fire was extinguished quickly, causing little damage.
The suspect, identified by police as Jairus Godeka, 38, briefly took a woman hostage, but police were able to persuade him to surrender peacefully, Madison said.
Godeka, a Kenyan national with legal resident status, had a history of disputes with the church and was charged earlier this year with attempting to blackmail church officials, Madison said.
He was being held pending probable charges of attempted aggravated murder, Madison said.
Church officials denounced the attack as a "sick hate crime."
"There's a lesson here and the lesson is about the damage religious hate-mongers cause," said a statement issued by the Church of Scientology International in Los Angeles.

A Scientology spokeswoman said three of the victims were local church ministers, including its executive director, while the fourth was identified as a 24-year-old man visiting from Clearwater, Florida.
The religion, founded in 1954 based on the writings of L. Ron Hubbard, claims more than 8 million adherents.
